Source: A 23-year-old woman presents to labor and delivery at 40 weeks gestation with abdominal contractions and leakage of fluid from her vagina.
Her cranial nerve exam is unremarkable and she has normal strength and sensation.
She subsequently undergoes an uncomplicated vaginal delivery.
There is blood in her vagina and her uterus is contracted.
While holding her newborn, the mother endorses a headache, blurry vision, and abdominal pain.
Physical exam reveals an uncomfortable woman.
Her temperature is 98.0°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 194/104 mmHg, pulse is 100/min, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air.
